title: A wider study pool. A sharper test.
summary: We screened 19 street-reallocation cases in 13 cities and expanded actual data acquisition in eight cities. Downloaded records and published tables are separately labeled below. They improve measurement, but do not yet identify a causal effect on total person flow or complete journey time.

findings.label: Geographic expansion
findings.detail: 19 screened cases, including related designs and explicit exclusions. New acquisition packages cover eight cities; eligibility and causal readiness are separate.

findings.label: Observed outcomes
findings.detail: Large treated-route cycling gains can coexist with rerouting, slower driving or faster buses. Keep each outcome visible.

findings.label: Causal all-mode estimate
findings.detail: Raw data and controlled studies improve the starting point. Passenger loads, comparable boundaries and credible counterfactuals remain gates.

cases.project: Bloor Street West pilot, Shaw Street to Avenue Road
cases.eligibility: Verified moving-lane reallocation; audit block and time-of-day geometry before pooling.
cases.status: Downloaded before/after volumes and driving times; descriptive network evidence
cases.treatment: One through motor lane each direction at all hours after conversion. Before, curb parking allowed additional moving lanes primarily in peak direction during peak periods; off-peak capacity therefore was not a simple four-to-two conversion. Turn lanes and later signal timing changes were included.
cases.measurement: June 2016, October 2016, June 2017. Three consecutive weekdays per corridor, 24-hour video at 11 sites; GPS driving runs on three weekdays per corridor in AM/midday/PM. Additional open-data 15-minute intersection turning counts around Bloor, Dupont and Harbord acquired; these queried records are not verified as the original 11-site pilot observations.
cases.identification: Dupont/Harbord are plausible spillover roads, not untreated controls. Danforth is used only for the separate economic study.
cases.finding: Bloor bicycles 3309 to 4925 (+48.84%); motor vehicles 24322 to 20434 (-15.99%). Sum of Bloor/Dupont/Harbord corridor-average bicycle counts 8896 to 9267 (+4.17%); corresponding motor count index 58315 to 56478 (-3.15%). Bloor peak-direction driving +120 seconds AM and +255 seconds PM.
cases.limit: Each corridor count is an average across separate sites. Sum is a count index, not an audited common screenline, unique people or journeys. Only three measurement waves; raw daily site records have not been obtained. Weather, ongoing background changes and signal retiming remain confounders. 49% includes Bay Street; 56% excludes the Bay site outside the pilot. Dry-day-only reported increase is nearly 70%. These are different estimands, not interchangeable. Attachment gives October Bloor vehicles 19918; main report gives 19919. This reconstruction consistently uses Attachment 1.

cases.eligibility: Verified moving-lane reallocation; audit block and time-of-day geometry before pooling.
cases.status: Downloaded daily directional bike/pedestrian/vehicle records; official bicycle counterfactual reported but not independently replicated
cases.treatment: West curb vehicle lane became southbound bicycle lane, east sidewalk became northbound bicycle path, pedestrians consolidated on west sidewalk. Connecting street and turn changes co-occurred.
cases.timing: 2009-07-13; Opened Monday morning July 13; installation July 10-13
cases.measurement: 579 calendar dates; valid total bicycles 562 days beginning June 16, pedestrians 548 beginning June 30, vehicles 523 beginning June 1. Only 25 bike/11 pedestrian/30 vehicle valid days before opening, including installation dates. Extended 2009–2012 daily bicycle records and 2008/2011 TransLink screenline/occupancy tables now acquired.
cases.identification: Ontario Bike Route was used in the City's bicycle model; Granville Bridge was monitored for diversion. Neither independent raw comparison series nor passenger counts acquired.
cases.finding: Six complete date pairs: July 2,3,4,6,7,9 versus July 16,17,18,20,21,23. Daily mean bicycles 3713.67 to 5527.67 (+48.85%), pedestrians 2362.33 to 2647.83 (+12.09%), vehicles 65127.33 to 65114.33 (-0.02%). Not causal. Immediate four-weekday sensitivity gives bicycles +108.58% and vehicles -5.50%, demonstrating substantial window sensitivity.
cases.limit: Very short usable before period; no seasons of pre-trends. Primary comparison uses six matched days, no weather control, and excludes holiday/fireworks pairs and all-mode missing observations. Vehicles are not people. New 2008/2011 occupancy and passenger tables add context, but road counts span 16 hours and transit counts 9 hours; they cannot be summed into a common-window total. Canada Line opening is a major co-intervention. Aligned other-crossing daily counts are still missing. Sixteen dates/modes have directional sums differing from source totals; original totals retained and discrepancies audited. Whole 2009-10 series crosses Olympics and transport/network changes; a full-period interrupted-time-series regression would be badly confounded without further work. The extended bicycle source disagrees with the original on 2010-06-29 (40,358 versus 4,420); the discrepancy is preserved and flagged.

cases.project: Massachusetts Avenue: Dudley St–Alewife Brook Parkway
cases.eligibility: Moving-lane loss documented: 2 each direction → 1 each direction.
cases.treatment: Conventional bike lanes upgraded to separated lanes; moving space also reallocated to bus lanes; bike plus bus and signals
cases.timing: Nov–early Dec 2021; construction started Nov 8. Roads Nov2–4 vsDec14–16 2021; Apr30–May9 2019 vsMay3–12 2022 Tue–Thu. Buses May2019/May2022. Bike peak-hour counts May2019/May2022.
cases.measurement: Original evaluation tables plus raw Miovision intersection counts, selected MBTA AVL event records and historical APC boarding/alighting/onboard-load records acquired. Download includes exact query windows, source metadata and audit notes.
cases.identification: Controlled descriptive before/after. No verified parallel pre-trends or uncertainty estimates; pandemic comparison and package treatment. Broadway Quincy–Prospect (nonparallel roadway chosen to avoid diversion); road times only
cases.finding: Mass Ave full-day motor time NB5.7→5.0min and SB4.9→4.7min in 2019/2022; PM8.0→8.2 and5.2→5.4. Published bus full-day summary−23%inbound/−40%outbound. Bike AM243→267,PM216→241.
cases.limit: The intervention combines bus and bike lanes. Miovision source identifiers use UTC timestamps while provisional clock-hour parsing did not; new rush-hour/count comparisons are withheld pending local-time normalization and padded date retrieval. MBTA APC seasonal averages are not matched-day passenger loads. RITIS individual road-time histories and car occupancy remain missing. No new aligned all-mode or complete-journey result is claimed.

cases.project: 2020 popup bicycle lanes, multiple arterial streets
cases.eligibility: Moving-road-space reallocation documented; exact segment dates and geometry require final audit.
cases.status: Raw motor sample and coverage audit completed; full causal replication and all-person flow unresolved
cases.treatment: Motor travel lane converted to bicycle lane
cases.timing: 2020-03-25 to 2020-07-07. Staggered street-specific dates in paper Figure 2; exact segments and extensions still require as-built audit
cases.measurement: Acquired all 24 monthly motor archives for 2019–2020: 4,532,392 hourly cross-section records. Published daily panel: 190,837 rows; candidate-road hourly extract: 309,085 rows. Bicycle archive: 456,118 counter-hour cells with provider quality flags preserved; 409,245 are unflagged numeric observations. Weather and project geometry also acquired.
cases.identification: Published station/date/hour fixed effects and event study; 23 treated stations on six streets vs 192 controls; nearby stations excluded. New replication should use modern staggered treatment estimators, strict pretrend and spillover tests.
cases.finding: Adjusted motor point speed coefficient −4.123 km/h; log speed −0.122 (~−11.5%). Log lane-average volume −0.00540, statistically inconclusive. These are reported published results, not newly replicated.
cases.limit: COVID demand and recovery coincide with treatment; political selection and parallel trends need scrutiny Paper averages lane volumes, not whole-road total; measurement target differs from all-person flow 2022 official metadata flags some motor detectors deinstalled for Radspur (bike lane), with removal dates blank 2025 archive reprocessing may differ from author data; do not mix quality regimes No transit loads or complete journey times Existing bicycle counters are approximately 1.55–1.97 km from the three verified popup geometries; motor and bicycle counts cannot be added as an aligned crossing. Candidate-road matches are not verified treatment assignments. New archives have not yet been used to replicate the published model.
cases.priority: High: motor outcome replication; insufficient for all-person flow

cases.project: CS6 Blackfriars and CS3 Victoria Embankment (2016)
cases.eligibility: Moving-lane replacement documented in official scheme drawings; not a uniform four-to-two conversion.
cases.treatment: Protected cycling, junctions, turn bans, signals and bus-stop changes.
cases.measurement: TfL cycling survey source files acquired for 23 waves across 2014–2017 (2,021,712 rows), including private/hire split, bridge/corridor extracts and comparison bridges. DfT estimation flags remain separately audited. Post-opening peak northbound report: cycle track 1,938 people/hour; main carriageway 1,542.
cases.identification: Descriptive early monitoring. No retrieved aligned comparison group/person-flow panel. ANPR link times, incomplete NS due camera failure. EW table is predictions vs observed, not before/after.
cases.finding: At this post-opening point and hour, the cycle track carried more people than the remaining main carriageway. TfL’s +5% initial throughput claim averages two locations; its before/after calculation was not reproducible from retrieved attachments.
cases.limit: No independently reproducible 5% calculation from retrieved FOI Peak point flow does not establish full-day/network flow Car/bus occupancy uncertainty unresolved Journeys can divert; rail/walking not aligned Several interventions simultaneous; full door-to-door time not observed DfT pre-2016 bridge estimates extrapolated from2011; north approach2015-2024 extrapolated2014; duplicate adjacent links cannot be independent observations DfT bike counts may miss new separated alignments; point58306 reports1bike in2018 so coverage needs physical audit Newly acquired 16-hour survey waves can combine different clock-hour slots observed on different dates, so they are not complete independent daily counts. The raw passenger-occupancy inputs behind the reported +5% throughput claim remain unacquired.

cases.project: Oxford Road / Cross City Bus Priority Package
cases.eligibility: Bundled corridor reallocation with bus gates and changes to a parallel road. Keep separate from bike-only conversion.
cases.treatment: 4.5km segregated on-carriageway cycle lanes plus1.6km bus/taxi/cycle-only section; general traffic excluded06:00-21:00; wider pavements; adjacent Upper Brook capacity expansion
cases.timing: Main enforcement September 2017; bus June 2013 vs June 2018, bike March 2015 vs March 2019.
cases.measurement: Bus running times, cycle/pedestrian counts, seven years of cycling totals, and GPS times on diversion road versus four radial comparators.
cases.identification: Before/after counts and observed bus times; adjacent-road GPS comparison versus four traffic-weighted radials. No randomization, no multi-period pre-trend test, no unit-level uncertainty. Through-trip estimates remove an assumed11-minute interchange allowance after new through-service; this is bundled transit benefit, not direct observed door-to-door panel.
cases.finding: Cycling counts rose at all four main sites. MRI-to-city local buses became 16.2% slower in the AM and 15.2% slower in the PM; reverse-direction changes were small. Estimated through-trip benefits also include removal of an assumed interchange penalty.
cases.limit: Does not establish total all-mode person throughput Bus, access restrictions, speed limit30to20mph and signal changes simultaneous Upper Brook capacity expanded deliberately; parallel road not untreated Cycle/walk comparisons one day each; adjacent cycle surveys different seasons Cycle site totals double-count riders Source table4.10 PM percentage says−20%, but40:38to29:25 calculates−27.6%; calculations preserve rawtimes andflag discrepancy Source table5.13 identical PM comparator series inbound/outbound; retain as published pending raw-data audit Reportsection7.1 explicitly no full post-implementation appraisal due absent without-scheme highwaysmodel

cases.project: Rue de Rivoli, site 10004 at 88 rue de Rivoli / Nicolas Flamel
cases.eligibility: Moving-road-space reallocation documented; exact segment dates and geometry require final audit.
cases.status: Post-treatment multimodal sample acquired and schema verified; excluded from causal before/after estimate
cases.treatment: Motor carriageway reallocation plus restriction of ordinary through motor traffic
cases.timing: 2020-05-11 to 2020-05-11. Policy commencement; phased physical works need exact segment audit
cases.measurement: Hourly thermal-camera bicycle, scooter, powered-two-wheeler, light vehicle, heavy vehicle, bus/coach counts Direction and entry-exit lane trajectory at one camera Same-site, same-hour modal classification Historical 2016–2020 bicycle and road-loop archives now downloaded, with selected Rivoli/Voltaire bicycle rows published and original archive hashes/URLs retained.
cases.identification: Cannot run before/after May2020 with this feed alone. Use for occupancy sensitivity and later interventions after verifying stable camera geometry; acquire older pre-treatment manual/loop counts and matched unaffected corridors.
cases.finding: A full 168-hour post-opening week was downloaded, with six vehicle classes and no duplicate record keys. This camera starts after the intervention, so it cannot supply the missing baseline.
cases.limit: First camera observations occur after intervention Treatment also restricts general traffic and occurs during COVID; cannot isolate cycle-lane effect nb_usagers means vehicles, not people Vehicle classification and site geometry evolve; missing category-hour rows must not be silently treated as observed zeros Do not sum cameras in series or infer metro diversion from street counts Rivoli bicycle counter location changes between the early and later archives; 2018 has no selected Rivoli observations. Road-loop occupancy is detector occupancy, not car passenger occupancy. Historical archives require quality and geometry alignment before any effect estimate.
cases.priority: High for aligned multimodal measurement; fails pre-treatment baseline in this feed

cases.eligibility: Related bundled street reallocation. Road space was narrowed for cycling and motor access restricted; a uniform moving-lane removal count has not been certified. Keep outside the clean lane-conversion cohort.
cases.treatment: Cycle space widening, two bus-only links, turn restrictions, stops and signal changes, and a bus-route change.
cases.timing: Trial began 1 October 2008. Bus GPS compares weeks 36–38 with 44–46; short adaptation window.
cases.measurement: Automatic bus running times for three routes; GPS cycling segment times; bicycle/vehicle counts and parallel-street diversion. Bus passenger totals were not resolved in this report.
cases.identification: Before/after evaluation, with seasonal cautions; no credible untreated comparison in the extracted running-time tables.
cases.finding: All eight 5A/350S route-period means fell by 13–84 seconds. Cycling segment means were mixed (−8 to +38 seconds); rerouted 3A also had mixed results.
cases.limit: Bus benefits cannot be assigned to bike lanes separately from bus priority and access restrictions. No matched total-person-flow or complete door-to-door time result. One printed bus difference is arithmetically inconsistent with its displayed means; corrected explicitly in our extract.
cases.priority: Useful bus and bike time benchmark

cases.eligibility: Moving-lane loss documented: Motor-road segments; exact counts not verified in accessed excerpt → Road space reallocated to separated bike lanes; exact counts not verified.
cases.treatment: COVID temporary lanes made permanent in2020; motor lane to bike
cases.timing: 2020; segment activation dates not recovered. October2019 vsOctober2021
cases.measurement: Primary publisher abstract/sections retrieved; cites SIMUR public Bluetooth speed data. Underlying files and full model not downloaded.
cases.identification: Peer-reviewed spatial before/after analysis; two October waves spanning pandemic. Full model, treatment dates, pretrends and standard errors not reproduced. Unmodified roads with spatial autoregressive models; nearby and farther roads considered
cases.finding: Maximum reported treated-road speed reduction4.5km/h(19%); some parallel-road speeds increased. Maximum is not network average.
cases.limit: pandemic changes; two months do not establish pre-trends; nearby roads may be affected not valid controls; unmeasured minor roads; speed alone is not person flow. Retrieve SIMUR Bluetooth historical links/observations and full paper/table specifications; verify exact 2020 links, add additional premonths and transit loads.

cases.eligibility: Mixed or unverified moving-lane treatment. Keep outside the strict cohort until segment geometry is audited.
cases.status: Downloaded official 2016 final report and reproduced selected counts/times
cases.treatment: Mixed network intervention; protected corridors plus shared space
cases.timing: 2015-06-18; Network open by June 18; individual components opened earlier
cases.measurement: September 2014 baseline and September 2016 final waves, plus interim/winter monitoring. Automated bike counters; manual volumes and GPS/stopwatch driving each collected on a single day per evaluation period. Annual 2012–2019 downtown cordon records and original workbooks also acquired, with person/mode definitions recorded. These cover a wider boundary than the project count sites.
cases.identification: Annual downtown cordon counts could supply broader all-mode outcomes, but a credible untreated comparison and date/boundary audit are still needed.
cases.finding: 5 Street CPR underpass 16h bicycles 630 to 2040 (+223.81%); 12 Avenue west of 2 Street 190 to 870 (+357.89%); 8 Avenue west of 3 Street 920 to 1240 (+34.78%). Driving: 5 Street PM 360 to 370 seconds; 12 Avenue AM 340 to 430, PM 690 to 440; 8 Avenue AM 330 to 315, PM 330 to 330. 12 Avenue PM baseline flagged by City as likely construction delayed.
cases.limit: Shared Stephen Avenue is not the same treatment as removal of moving lanes and must be separated. Single-day manual/GPS waves are vulnerable to weather, construction and sampling variation. Concurrent changes in employment and spending are acknowledged by the report. Network bike totals may count repeat/cross-corridor trips; do not call them unique riders or additional trips. A citywide cordon series is not an untreated comparator or a bike-lane-specific causal estimate.

cases.eligibility: Verified moving-lane reallocation; audit block and time-of-day geometry before pooling.
cases.status: Adverse historical observation; short pilot, not a generalizable causal estimate
cases.treatment: One northbound moving lane closed to create bike lane; southbound cycling stayed on sidewalk
cases.measurement: Shows a directly relevant unfavorable case with reported occupant/person counts, avoiding selection of successful cases only.
cases.identification: No credible concurrent untreated comparison identified; Environment Week timing and rapid adaptation matter.
cases.finding: City reported +870 cyclists/day (+39%), -8800 car occupants/day (-9%) and 7500 fewer people crossing per day; early delays up to 20 minutes diminished during week, bus delays 3-4 minutes. Underlying Appendix C table was not available in retrieved HTML, so these are reported results, not reconstructed totals.
cases.limit: Only one week, with a different direction/design from the 2009 trial. Cannot interpret the negative bridge total as a citywide mobility loss without network/OD counts. Short-run disruption must not be pooled with mature lane operation.

cases.project: Dunsmuir Street protected two-way bike lane
cases.eligibility: Verified moving-lane reallocation; audit block and time-of-day geometry before pooling.
cases.status: Official design and monitoring reports; raw multimodal panel not acquired
cases.treatment: Three westbound moving lanes reduced to two
cases.measurement: Verified moving-lane reallocation, continuous all-bike counting and official driving-time monitoring.
cases.identification: Nearby routes share the growing downtown cycling network and may experience diversion; require independent untreated comparison.
cases.finding: Published reports describe growing cycling and little change in general traffic volumes/times; some rerouted trips to northern Hornby blocks take approximately 90 seconds longer. No independent all-person treatment effect computed.
cases.limit: Do not conflate Dunsmuir Street with Dunsmuir Viaduct: the viaduct lane was already closed by construction barriers before the bike-lane conversion. Network co-interventions and 2010 transport disruptions complicate isolated attribution. Vehicle counts do not measure passenger totals.

cases.project: Hornby Street protected two-way bike lane
cases.eligibility: Mixed or unverified moving-lane treatment. Keep outside the strict cohort until segment geometry is audited.
cases.status: Treatment-screening caution; exclude full corridor from clean moving-lane pool
cases.measurement: Useful network mechanism/route diversion evidence after separating treatment segments.
cases.finding: Design retains two travel lanes on most blocks by removing parking; southern Pacific-to-Davie segment proposes removal of a travel lane. Whole-corridor results would mix these treatment types.
cases.limit: Do not use whole Hornby corridor as proof about converting a moving lane. As-built geometry on southern segment needs verification before eligibility.

cases.project: Burrard Bridge renewal and north intersection redesign
cases.eligibility: Verified moving-lane reallocation; audit block and time-of-day geometry before pooling.
cases.status: Confirmed treatment package; suitable post-period multimodal panel not acquired
cases.treatment: Northbound moving lane to cycling, plus bridge approach widening and turn/intersection changes
cases.timing: 2017; Completion year confirmed; exact full reopening date not primary-source verified here
cases.measurement: Potential longer bike count history and documented geometry; not yet a completed new causal estimate.
cases.finding: No reconstructed post-2017 effect. 2015 proposal combines midspan moving-lane reduction with widening roughly 100m of approach to preserve intersection capacity, so evaluation would estimate a package rather than isolated lane removal.
cases.limit: Downloaded 2009-2010 all-mode counts do not cover this intervention. Long construction period, rehabilitation and intersection widening co-occur. Do not count 2009 and 2017 as independent cases without modeling shared corridor history.

cases.eligibility: Moving-road-space reallocation documented; exact segment dates and geometry require final audit.
cases.status: Treatment verified, acquisition candidate only; no computed causal effect
cases.treatment: Protected cycle tracks with motor carriageway/capacity reduction; bus-stop and streetscape changes
cases.timing: 2017-07-01 to 2019-07-01. Month precision; dates use day01 placeholders. Staged sections through July2019; need exact segment opening dates.
cases.measurement: Official construction staging and final cross-section description 2017 project presentation includes baseline motor traffic and forecast capacity change Historical 2016–2020 bicycle and road-loop archives now downloaded, with selected Rivoli/Voltaire bicycle rows published and original archive hashes/URLs retained.
cases.identification: Proposed, not yet run; no aligned panel acquired. Segment-level staggered before/after with adjacent diversion screenline and matched untreated arterials; distinguish construction from permanent opening.
cases.finding: Treatment staging and historical archives are acquired; a validated aligned outcome panel and causal comparison have not yet been assembled.
cases.limit: Final street has one moving lane per direction except two-lane intersection approaches; exact baseline lane counts must be digitized segment by segment The cited 20% capacity reduction is a forecast in the project presentation, not an observed flow estimate Bus islands and other streetscape changes make treatment a bundle Thermal multimodal feed begins too late for 2017 baseline; older loop/bike archives require joining Rivoli bicycle counter location changes between the early and later archives; 2018 has no selected Rivoli observations. Road-loop occupancy is detector occupancy, not car passenger occupancy. Historical archives require quality and geometry alignment before any effect estimate.
cases.priority: Medium: pre-COVID alternative, data alignment not certified

cases.eligibility: Moving-lane loss documented: 4 through lanes,total → 2 through lanes,total,+center turn lane.
cases.treatment: Added ClassII bike lanes both sides; bike plus turn lane and signals
cases.timing: August2014 (construction phase timing varies). May2013 before andOct2014 after:4 vs2 weekdays of bike/ped observations per CARB technical reanalysis
cases.measurement: Primary university abstract retrieved; publisher full text not obtained. State technical reanalysis documents lane conversion and sampling.
cases.identification: Before/after observational field study; several signals and turn changes bundled. Short unmatched seasonal windows. No contemporaneous comparison group verified from accessed primary abstract; do not assume one
cases.finding: Primary authors report243%average intersection bicycle growth and statistically significant evening-peak car travel-time decrease; numerical car-time estimate not recovered.
cases.limit: route diversion can explain corridor bike gains; May vsOctober season/academic calendar; no verified control/pretrend; signal/turn-lane cointerventions; small university city transportability. Obtain author paper/data, actual car run times, diversion-route counts and occupancy before quantitative pooling.

cases.eligibility: Moving-lane loss documented: 2 through+1 drive/left-turn lane; separate bus lane → 2 through+left-turn/parking; separate bus lane.
cases.treatment: One-way conventional bike lane replaced by two-way protected lane; bike plus signals and direction change
cases.timing: September8,2014. Bike July29–Aug23 2014 baseline vsannual postaverage; road and bus windows vary
cases.measurement: 18page official evaluation search-index accessible; directPDFdownload403. Public bike counter exists but beginsnearopening. Public Second Avenue and Fremont hourly counters plus selected motor count bins acquired. The Second Avenue retrieved series begins in 2015 and supplies no pre-opening 2014 baseline.
cases.identification: Agency before/after with short bike baseline; intersection signals, two-way permission and bikeshare concurrent. Bus travel-time comparisons3rd/5th Avenue mixed results; not full all-mode counterfactual
cases.finding: Report bicycles188→744dailyaverage using mismatched windows; vehicle volumes increased; bus travel-time changes mostlyunder1minute. Do not treat bicycle ratio as induced net cycling.
cases.limit: one-way to two-way changes counting opportunity; short seasonal baseline; Pronto bike-share opening; no systempersonflow; annual motor/bike windows differ. Recover evaluation underlying motor/AVL records and consistent comparison counts; validate treatment geometry by block.

cases.project: West Marginal Way SW,SW MarginalPl–south ofSW IdahoSt,0.4mile
cases.eligibility: Moving-lane loss documented: Two southbound locally, but one-lane bottlenecks already present north/south → One southbound plus two-way protectedbike lane.
cases.treatment: Duwamish Trail missing link; bike plus safety changes
cases.measurement: Primary SDOT summary, selected motor count bins and nearby Spokane Street hourly counter records acquired. The Spokane counter is a different measurement boundary; it is not a substitute for West Marginal same-site counts.

cases.finding: Agency reports weekday bikes+144%,weekend+53%,southbound motor travel timeincrease<1second. Inputs/windowalignment not reproduced.

cases.eligibility: Excluded from strict conversion cohort: moving-lane loss unverified.
cases.status: method comparator excluded from strict pool
cases.identification: Longitudinalcontrolledobservationalpanel;attrition and other transportchanges. Residentpanel southCBDnearcycleway vswestCBD
cases.finding: Primaryauthorpanel study gives method for following travelers across modes, but moving-laneremoval unverified. Do not count as eligiblelaneconversion.

studies.name: Provisional COVID-19 infrastructure induces large, rapid increases in cycling (2021)
studies.coverage: 106 European cities. 736 bicycle counters; 2020 COVID rollout
studies.finding: Abstract: 11–48% increase in cycling across specifications; not an all-mode result.
studies.limit: Mixed/uncertified: underlying policy data cannot systematically distinguish implementation types. Cycling-only counts do not establish mode substitution or total persons/time. COVID and dense-city context constrain transport. Berlin overlaps this sample; do not double-count as independent evidence. Archive acquired and checksum verified, but advertised panel is a Git LFS pointer. Linked repository/object returned 404. No model reproduced.

studies.name: The Causal Effect of Cycling Infrastructure on Traffic and Accidents: Evidence from Pop-Up Bike Lanes in Berlin (2022)
studies.coverage: Berlin. 23 treated sensors in six streets versus 192 controls; 2019–2020 hourly traffic data, selected weekday/daytime coverage.
studies.outcome: Motor detector speed, Motor detector volume, Accidents
studies.finding: Adjusted Table 1: speed −4.123 km/h; log speed −0.122; log volume −0.0054 (not statistically significant).
studies.limit: Yes: motor moving lanes replaced by cycle lanes. Paper averages volume and speed across lanes: full cross-section flow must be independently reconstructed. Official metadata identifies cycle-lane detector deinstallations; post-treatment sensor completeness requires audit. Spot speed is not journey time; no aligned bicycle/transit/person outcome. Official raw sensor files acquired separately by Europe workstream; no verified processed replication package found. Published estimates not reproduced.

studies.name: Heterogeneous impacts of protected bike lanes on bikeshare behavior across demographic groups in New York (2026)
studies.coverage: New York City. 72 million selected Citi Bike trips; source data span 2013–2024.
studies.finding: Authors report 379 additional rides per station-month after protected-lane installation (p<0.001); painted-lane causal effect not detected.
studies.limit: Not established: lane type is classified, but loss of motor moving lanes is a separate eligibility question. Bike-share starts are not all bicycle crossings or total mobility. Matching observed neighborhood characteristics does not establish exogenous placement. Staggered TWFE requires heterogeneous-effect and spillover audit. Full primary article acquired. Availability statement links public raw Citi Bike and NYC bike-lane data; no processed panel or code repository identified in article. No model reproduced.

studies.name: Cycling infrastructure and its co-benefits: Evidence from a longitudinal natural experiment (2026)
studies.coverage: Montréal region. 2.5 km protected lanes; longitudinal intervention/control surveys in 2023 and 2024.
studies.outcome: Self-reported weekly mode-use shares, Safety and neighborhood perceptions
studies.finding: Driving share decreased significantly; cycling and walking share increases were not significant.
studies.limit: Unverified; abstract notes on-street parking removal as possible mechanism. No verified moving-lane loss. Shares are not person-throughput levels or complete journey time. Sample size, attrition, parallel trends and data access require full-text review before causal weighting. No downloadable analysis panel acquired; abstract only verified.

studies.name: Does new bicycle infrastructure result in new or rerouted bicyclists? A longitudinal GPS study in Oslo (2019)
studies.coverage: Oslo. 113 GPS-app participants; published exposed/quasi-control comparison groups include 39 and 47 people.
studies.outcome: Route choice, Cycling mode share, Route deviation
studies.finding: Treated-route cycling increased while parallel-route cycling declined; cycling mode-share change was not statistically significant.
studies.limit: Not verified. Small selected app panel. Route substitution warns against equating a treated counter increase with net new cyclists. Not an all-mode throughput estimate. No replication panel acquired.

studies.name: All ages and abilities cycling infrastructure, cycling activity, and perceived safety: Findings from a natural experiment study in three mid-sized Canadian cities (2023)
studies.coverage: Victoria, with Kelowna and Halifax comparisons. 33 km AAA network; repeated population surveys in 2016, 2019 and 2021, roughly 1000 per city-wave.
studies.finding: No statistically different cycling change for proximity comparison; control-city investment and COVID complicate inference.
studies.limit: Mixed network; not certified moving-lane conversions. Control contamination. COVID and delayed completion. No vehicle/transit throughput or full journey outcome. Primary indexed article says authors cannot share data.

studies.name: Have paved trails and protected bike lanes led to more bicycling in Atlanta? A generalized synthetic-control analysis (2022)
studies.coverage: Atlanta. Five infrastructure groups; monthly Strava 2016-10 to 2018-09 calibrated using 15 physical counters.
studies.finding: Joint ratio 1.10 (95% CI 0.99–1.18) for narrower treatment definition; effects differ by project.
studies.limit: Mixed off-street trails and protected bike lanes; not certified conversion subset. App sample and calibration may not represent all trips. Counter calibration does not identify car/transit substitution. Bicycle-distance is a distinct outcome from crossings, trips, or time. No analysis data acquired.

strategy.title: Separate policy classes before estimating
strategy.detail: Build a strict moving-lane conversion cohort, a bike-and-bus redesign cohort, and a mechanism-only group. Verify as-built lanes, opening dates and construction windows by segment. Parking-only projects do not answer the same question.

strategy.title: Prioritize three complementary panels
strategy.detail: Vancouver for all-bike, pedestrian and vehicle counts at one boundary; Toronto for route diversion; Berlin for high-frequency motor counts and speeds with control sites. Cambridge and Manchester strengthen bus and network-time measurement. No city currently supplies every required outcome.

strategy.title: Measure the network, including subway substitution
strategy.detail: Use a fixed, nonduplicating boundary across affected routes. Add onboard bus and rail passengers crossing it, observed vehicle occupancy and all-bike/pedestrian counts in the same hours. Station entries and boardings are not onboard boundary loads.

strategy.title: Make the counterfactual pass explicit tests
strategy.detail: Select untreated roads by pre-treatment demand, capacity and trends; use modern staggered adoption or synthetic-control designs, placebo dates, alternative donors and spillover buffers. Cluster at the corridor/network intervention level. Nearby diversion routes are outcomes, not automatic controls.

strategy.title: Keep journey time and access as separate outcomes
strategy.detail: Follow fixed origin–destination and time-of-day cohorts across mode changes. Include access, waiting and transfer time; report person-weighted mean and reliability. Report completed trips and access alongside total minutes so suppressed travel cannot masquerade as a benefit.

strategy.title: Pool only after measurement and identification pass
strategy.detail: No common causal estimate is produced yet. After passing gates, pool compatible within-city effects with uncertainty and leave-one-city-out checks; account for shared datasets and report heterogeneity by transit supply, occupancy, baseline congestion, weather and adaptation. Reweight to NYC only where those conditions overlap.

acquisition.summary: This audit separates actual downloads, published table extracts, sources located and remaining gaps. The new acquisition pass covers eight cities. These are source families and bounded extracts, not a claim that every potentially useful dataset is available or that a causal effect has been estimated.

records.dataset: DWD daily weather, station 00433
records.usable_for: Weather covariates for aligned daily panels.
records.limitation: Rainfall missing on two days; station is a city weather proxy. Weather adjustment alone does not resolve treatment confounding.
records.next_requirement: Join only after spatial treatment and timing are established.

records.dataset: Official bicycle workbook with provider quality flags
records.coverage: 2019–2020; 26 directional counters; 19,006 counter-days
records.usable_for: Quality-aware cycling baseline and seasonal comparison.
records.limitation: 46,793 provider-flagged zero/implausible cells and 80 other missing cells. Naive clock labels require DST audit. Existing counters are not on the three verified project screenlines.
records.next_requirement: Obtain counters at treated boundaries and comparable untreated sites.

records.dataset: Official hourly motor detection archive
records.rows: 4,532,392 hourly records; 190,837 published section-days; 309,085 candidate-road hours
records.coverage: 2019-01-01–2020-12-31; 24 monthly archives; 267 cross-sections
records.usable_for: Pre-period, road volumes, point speeds and comparison-road candidates. Attribution: Digitale Plattform Stadtverkehr Berlin / Verkehrsdetektion Berlin.
records.limitation: Vehicles are not people; road-name candidate assignment is unverified. Missing full-source dates 2019-06-03 and 2019-09-10. Point speed is not complete journey time.
records.next_requirement: Verify historical treatment geometry, same-screenline bike counters and occupancy/passenger data.

records.dataset: Official project pages and current infrastructure geometry
records.rows: 3 verified pop-up project geometries plus detector-proximity audit
records.coverage: 2020 project documents; current mapped geometry
records.usable_for: Treatment-location screening and identification of missing screenline coverage.
records.limitation: Current shapes do not establish all historical lane configurations. Nearest bicycle counters are about 1.55–1.97 km from these three shapes.
records.next_requirement: Confirm dated as-built lane changes and match each sensor to its actual intervention.

records.coverage: 2020 intervention period discussed in the paper
records.usable_for: Potential road-speed panel
records.limitation: The source and published study were located; underlying historical observations and a complete replication have not been acquired.
records.next_requirement: Obtain dated link-level observations and treatment mapping.

records.limitation: Annual site summaries, not individual observations. Different sites surveyed on different days. Missing fields retained. Network and economic changes, weather and construction confound before/after comparisons.
records.next_requirement: Consistent boundary/site accounting, exact date alignment and untreated-city comparison.

records.next_requirement: Check changing cordon locations/methods and compare against employment, weather and control cities.
